title: Maximally monotone inclusion with an exact resolvent and selectable step size

assumptions.scope: All point pairs in the declared function domain. Blockwise constants are uniform in the remaining fixed variables.
assumptions.description: A maximal monotone; some zero z* satisfies ||z0−z*||≤R

model.parameter_domain_description: $R$: nonnegative real; $d$: positive integer; $\varepsilon$: positive real. Derived quantities are defined in the parameter table. Each region states any additional accuracy and dimension conditions.
description_paragraphs: The operator $A:\mathbb{R}^d\rightrightarrows\mathbb{R}^d$ is maximally monotone. A zero $z^\star$ satisfies $\|z_0-z^\star\|_2\le R$, and $R\ge0$ is public.

operations.order_convention: This operation is charged according to its explicit input and output, not renamed according to a scalar function's derivative order.

feedback_quality.description: Exact responses from the same hidden object fixed before interaction

operations.coupling: Deterministic exact responses with repeated queries allowed; stochastic sample-reuse permissions are irrelevant.

public_inputs: Public inputs comprise the dimension $d$ and parameters $R$ and $\varepsilon$, together with the stated initial point and feasible-set information. Analytic descriptions of hidden functions, operators, and matrices are not supplied.
description_paragraphs: Public inputs comprise the dimension $d$ and parameters $R$ and $\varepsilon$, together with the stated initial point and feasible-set information. Analytic descriptions of hidden functions, operators, and matrices are not supplied.
The algorithm may choose any positive real step size. The full resolvent is exact, and step-size bit length is free.

output.feasibility: Return $(\widehat z,\widehat v)\in\mathbb R^d\times\mathbb R^d$ satisfying $\widehat v\in A(\widehat z)$.
output.allowed_postprocessing: arbitrary measurable postprocessing; unqueried output permitted unless restriction says otherwise
output.certificate_requirement: Return $(z,v)$ with $v\in A(z)$. After one resolvent call, the certificate is $v=(u-z)/\eta$.
description_paragraphs: Return $(\widehat{z},\widehat{v})$ with $\widehat{v}\in A(\widehat{z})$ almost surely. The response $\widehat{z}=J_{\eta A}(z_0)$ determines $\widehat{v}=(z_0-\widehat{z})/\eta$.

description_paragraphs: Each full-resolvent query costs one call. If $R=0$, output $(z_0,0)$ without querying. If $R>0$, a single query at $\eta\ge R/\varepsilon$ suffices.
Use a fixed worst-case budget: calls never exceed the prespecified $N$ on any instance or random execution path. Earlier stopping within the budget is permitted.

Count all information calls for one instance and one requested accuracy, including initialization. Exact-real arithmetic, storage, and solving known models from public inputs and returned data are uncharged. This query-complexity quantity does not certify arithmetic or bit complexity.

bounds.derivation: Query $z=J_{\eta A}(z_0)$ and set $v=(z_0-z)/\eta$, giving $v\in A(z)$. Firm nonexpansiveness relative to a zero yields $\|z_0-z\|_2\le\|z_0-z^\star\|_2\le R$. The public step size $\eta=R/\varepsilon$ ensures $\|v\|_2\le\varepsilon$ using one exact resolvent call.
bounds.witness_type_note: The witnesses return either the public initial point or one exact resolvent query at a fixed step size. Neither uses private or oracle randomness.

bounds.derivation: On the real line take $A_\pm(z)=(2\varepsilon/R)(z\mp R)$ and $z_0=0$. The roots are $\pm R$. Residual at most $\varepsilon$ requires the output to lie within radius $R/2$ of the respective root. These success sets are disjoint, so one zero-query output distribution cannot attain probability $2/3$ on both instances.
bounds.lower_scope_type_note: Two-point testing, zero-query indistinguishability, and nonexistence counterexamples cover arbitrary privately randomized policies. These are not linear-span lower bounds.

proofs.title: single exact resolvent with eta=R/eps
proofs.body: Query $z=J_{\eta A}(z_0)$ and set $v=(z_0-z)/\eta$, giving $v\in A(z)$. Firm nonexpansiveness relative to a zero yields $\|z_0-z\|_2\le\|z_0-z^\star\|_2\le R$. The public step size $\eta=R/\varepsilon$ ensures $\|v\|_2\le\varepsilon$ using one exact resolvent call.
proofs.scope: All model, oracle, algorithm, guarantee, quantity, resource-projection, and region conditions attached to the mapped bounds remain in force.

Residual at most $\varepsilon$ requires the output to lie within radius $R/2$ of the respective root. These success sets are disjoint, so one zero-query output distribution cannot attain probability $2/3$ on both instances.

proofs.body: When the initialization radius is $R=0$, the promise gives $0\in A(z_0)$. Return the graph pair $(z_0,0)$ without a query. It has zero residual and satisfies the output requirement exactly.
